en: Oṃ, salutation be to the Supreme Self, whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss, whose essential form is composed of light, and who is the embodiment of all auspiciousness in the universe. ||1||
May Prakṛti, the five elements, the planets, the worlds, the vowels, the directions, and time always bring auspiciousness to all. || 2 ||
I bow to the Mother of Bhārata, whose feet are washed by oceans of jewels, who wears the Himalayas as her crown, and who is enriched by the jewels of Brahmins and royal sages. 3.
Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Himālaya—the soul of the gods—Raivataka, Vindhya, and likewise the Ārāvalī mountain, are to be meditated upon. ||4||
The Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Sindhu, Brahmaputra, Gaṇḍakī, Kāverī, Yamunā, Revā, Kṛṣṇā, Godā, and Mahānadī. ||5||
Ayodhyā, Mathurā, Māyā, Kāśī, Kāñcī, Avantikā, Vaiśālī, Dvārikā, the city of Takṣaśilā, and Gayā are to be meditated upon. ||6||
Prayāga, Pāṭaliputra, the great Vijayānagara, Indraprastha, Somanātha, and likewise the beloved Amṛtasaras; ||7||
The four Vedas, the Purāṇas, as well as all the Upaniṣads, the Rāmāyaṇa, the Mahābhārata, the Gītā, and the six systems of philosophy. ||8||
The Jaina scriptures, the Tripitaka, the Gurugrantha, and the words of the virtuous—this is the supreme treasury of knowledge, which should always be held with faith in the heart. (9)
Arundhatī, Anasūyā, Sāvitrī, Jānakī, Satī, Draupadī, Kṛṣṇā, Gārgī, Mīrā, and likewise Durgāvatī. ||10||
Having prostrated before the divine Mothers—Lakṣmī, Ahalyā, Cannammā, Rudramāmbā, Suvikramā, Niveditā, and Sāradā—[he offered his salutations]. 11.
Śrī Rāma, Bharata, Kṛṣṇa, Bhīṣma, Dharma, as well as Arjuna, Mārkaṇḍeya, Hariścandra, Prahlāda, Nārada, and Dhruva. ||12||
Hanumān, Janaka, Vyāsa, Vasiṣṭha, Śuka, Bali, Dadhīci, Viśvakarman, Pṛthu, Vālmīki, and Bhārgava. ||13||
Bhagīratha, Ekalavya, Manu, Dhanvantari, as well as Śibi and Rantideva—these are those whose glories are celebrated in the Purāṇas. ||14||
Buddha, Jinendra, Gorakṣa, Pāṇini, and Patañjali; Śaṅkara, Madhva, Nimbārka, Śrī Rāmānuja, and Vallabha. ||15||
Jhulelāl, Caitanya, Tiruvalluvar, the Nāyanmārs and Āḷvārs, Kaṃba, and Basaveśvara; ||16||
Devala, Ravidāsa, Kabīra, Guru Nānaka, Narasī, and Tulasīdāsa—these ten were of firm vows. ||17||
And Śrīmacchaṅkaradeva, Bandhūsāyana, Mādhava, Jñāneśvara, Tukārāma, Rāmadāsa, and Purandara; ||18||
May these—Birasā, Sahajānanda, and the great Ramānanda—always bestow the divine perfection of the six qualities. 19.
Ravivarmā in Bhātakhaṇḍa, that King Bhoja who was like the moon of fortune, and Kalāvant—these are renowned and should be remembered constantly. ||20||
The sage among the Bharatas, Kālidāsa, Śrībhoja, Janaka, Sūradāsa, Tyāgarāja, and the excellent poet Rasakhāna. ||21||
Agastya, Kaṃbu, Kauṇḍiṇya, Rājendra born of the Cōḷa lineage, Aśoka, Puṣyamitra, and the wise Khāravela. ||22||
Cāṇakya, Candragupta, Vikrama, Śālivāhana, Samudragupta, Śrīharṣa, Śaileṃdra, and Bapparāvala. ||23||
Lācit, Bhāskara-varman, Yaśodharman the conqueror of the Hūṇas, Śrī-Kṛṣṇa-devarāja, Lalitāditya, and Udbala; ||24||
Musunūri Nāyaka, Pratāpa Śivabhūpati, and Raṇajitasiṃha—these were heroes renowned for their valor. ||25||
And the scientists were Kapila, Kaṇāda, Śuśruta, as well as Caraka, Bhāskarācārya, and the wise Varāhamihira. ||26||
Nāgārjuna, Bharadvāja, Āryabhaṭṭa, Vasu, Budha, the venerable Veṅkaṭarāma, and the wise Rāmānuja are to be meditated upon. ||27||
Rāmakṛṣṇa, Dayānanda, Ravīndra, Rāmamohana, Rāmatīrtha, and Aravinda, as well as Vivekānanda of rising fame. ||28||
Dadābhāī Gopabandhu, Tilaka, Ādṛta Gāndhi, Rāmananda Mālavīya, and Śrī Subrahmaṇya Bhāratī. (29)
Subhāṣa, Praṇavānanda, Krāntivīra, Vināyaka, Ṭhakkara, Bhīmarāva, and Nārāyaṇa Phule were his gurus. ||30||
Keśava and Mādhava, the two who bestow power upon the Saṅgha, should always be remembered; they are the givers of ever-fresh consciousness. ||31||
Those devotees who have not been mentioned, whose hearts are attached to the feet of the Lord; those heroes who have not been specified, who have crushed their enemies on the battlefield;
those who are upholders of the assembly, and who are skilled in providing for the welfare of others through specialized knowledge.
May there be daily salutations to all those virtuous people. || 32 ||
Whoever should always recite this hymn on the Unity of the Self with faith shall remain steadfast in the duty of the nation and keep undivided Bhārata in mind. ||33||
I bow to the Mother of India.
